Most people building community go about it in the wrong order. They get the land first, then write the vision down in a document, then let whoever had the money end up owning it. And the emotional preparation? They'll do that later, when everyone has more time.

The better order is less cinematic, more like this: practice together, process a real conflict, clarify your values, test membership, decide ownership and exit, and only then think about land. I know, it wouldn't make much of a movie!

Most people building community go about it in the wrong order. They get the land first, then write the vision down in a document, then let whoever had the money end up owning it. And the emotional preparation? They'll do that later, when everyone has more time.

The better order is less cinematic, more like this: practice together, process a real conflict, clarify your values, test membership, decide ownership and exit, and only then think about land. I know, it wouldn't make much of a movie!

Likewise, the economic side should go in stages. You shouldn't try to fly straight to the economic destination! Only after the group has proven it can reliably provide for everybody, and fairly decide who gets what from the common, should it move to a common purse. And cutting back on outside money, or getting rid of it, should come from what the group has shown it can do. ("Money is impure!" is a weird thing to say while somebody else is quietly paying the tax bill.)

People sometimes buy forty acres and then bring all their unprocessed baggage with them to a more scenic location. The view's better, I'll give them that! But now the conflict has goats.

The inner pl/ork can start right where you live, though. Peer counseling only needs two people and enough privacy to talk. And reparenting, somatic work, jealousy, conflict repair, etc etc? None of that has to wait for a deed!
